claim: P-glycoprotein (Pgp) is a prototypical ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter of great biological and clinical significance.
source: P-glycoprotein (Pgp) is a prototypical ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter of great biological and clinical significance.
evidence: This is a general characterization statement supported by established scientific knowledge about Pgp.

claim: Pgp confers cancer multidrug resistance.
source: Pgp confers cancer multidrug resistance and mediates the bioavailability and pharmacokinetics of many drugs (Juliano and Ling, 1976; Ueda et al., 1986; Sharom, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research (Juliano and Ling, 1976; Ueda et al., 1986; Sharom, 2011).

claim: Pgp mediates the bioavailability and pharmacokinetics of many drugs.
source: Pgp confers cancer multidrug resistance and mediates the bioavailability and pharmacokinetics of many drugs (Juliano and Ling, 1976; Ueda et al., 1986; Sharom, 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research (Juliano and Ling, 1976; Ueda et al., 1986; Sharom, 2011).

claim: Decades of structural and biochemical studies have provided insights into how Pgp binds diverse compounds.
source: Decades of structural and biochemical studies have provided insights into how Pgp binds diverse compounds (Loo and Clarke, 2000; Loo et al., 2009; Aller et al., 2009; Alam et al., 2019; Nosol et al., 2020; Chufan et al., 2015), but how they are translocated through the membrane has remained elusive.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior structural and biochemical studies.

claim: How substrates are translocated through the membrane has remained elusive.
source: Decades of structural and biochemical studies have provided insights into how Pgp binds diverse compounds (Loo and Clarke, 2000; Loo et al., 2009; Aller et al., 2009; Alam et al., 2019; Nosol et al., 2020; Chufan et al., 2015), but how they are translocated through the membrane has remained elusive.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap in the field based on prior literature.

claim: The authors covalently attached a cyclic substrate to discrete sites of Pgp.
source: Here, we covalently attached a cyclic substrate to discrete sites of Pgp and determined multiple complex structures in inward- and outward-facing states by cryoEM.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The authors determined multiple complex structures in inward- and outward-facing states by cryoEM.
source: Here, we covalently attached a cyclic substrate to discrete sites of Pgp and determined multiple complex structures in inward- and outward-facing states by cryoEM.
evidence: This describes the structural data obtained in the study.

claim: The structures trace the substrate passage across the membrane.
source: In conjunction with molecular dynamics simulations, our structures trace the substrate passage across the membrane and identify conformational changes in transmembrane helix 1 (TM1) as regulators of substrate transport.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on the structural data and MD simulations.

claim: Conformational changes in transmembrane helix 1 (TM1) regulate substrate transport.
source: In conjunction with molecular dynamics simulations, our structures trace the substrate passage across the membrane and identify conformational changes in transmembrane helix 1 (TM1) as regulators of substrate transport.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on structural data and MD simulations.

claim: In mid-transport conformations, TM1 breaks at glycine 72.
source: In mid-transport conformations, TM1 breaks at glycine 72.
evidence: This is a specific structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: Mutation of glycine 72 significantly impairs drug transport of Pgp in vivo.
source: Mutation of this residue significantly impairs drug transport of Pgp in vivo, corroborating the importance of its regulatory role.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from in vivo drug transport assays.

claim: The cyclic substrate can exit Pgp without the requirement of a wide-open outward-facing conformation.
source: Importantly, our data suggest that the cyclic substrate can exit Pgp without the requirement of a wide-open outward-facing conformation, diverting from the common efflux model for Pgp and other ABC exporters.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the structural data and MD simulations.

claim: The proposed mechanism diverts from the common efflux model for Pgp and other ABC exporters.
source: Importantly, our data suggest that the cyclic substrate can exit Pgp without the requirement of a wide-open outward-facing conformation, diverting from the common efflux model for Pgp and other ABC exporters.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in the context of existing models.

claim: Pgp is highly expressed in the liver, kidney, and intestines.
source: Pgp is highly expressed in the liver, kidney, and intestines, where it limits absorption and enhances the excretion of cytotoxic compounds (Thiebaut et al., 1987; Cascorbi, 2011; Cordon-Cardo et al., 1990).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on Pgp expression patterns.

claim: Pgp limits absorption and enhances the excretion of cytotoxic compounds in the liver, kidney, and intestines.
source: Pgp is highly expressed in the liver, kidney, and intestines, where it limits absorption and enhances the excretion of cytotoxic compounds (Thiebaut et al., 1987; Cascorbi, 2011; Cordon-Cardo et al., 1990).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on Pgp function.

claim: In the blood-brain, blood-testis, and blood-placenta barriers, Pgp protects and detoxifies sanctuaries from xenobiotics.
source: In the blood-brain, blood-testis, and blood-placenta barriers, Pgp protects and detoxifies sanctuaries from xenobiotics (Schinkel, 1999; Borst and Schinkel, 2013; Fromm, 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on Pgp function in biological barriers.

claim: Pgp is a major determinant of drug bioavailability and pharmacokinetics.
source: Of central importance for many chemotherapeutic treatments, Pgp is a major determinant of drug bioavailability and pharmacokinetics and confers multidrug resistance in several diseases, most notably cancer (Szakács et al., 2006; Gottesman and Ling, 2006; Giacomini et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on Pgp's role in drug pharmacokinetics.

claim: Pgp confers multidrug resistance in several diseases, most notably cancer.
source: Of central importance for many chemotherapeutic treatments, Pgp is a major determinant of drug bioavailability and pharmacokinetics and confers multidrug resistance in several diseases, most notably cancer (Szakács et al., 2006; Gottesman and Ling, 2006; Giacomini et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on Pgp and multidrug resistance.

claim: Evasion, selective inhibition, and modulation of Pgp transport are important goals in drug development.
source: Consequently, evasion, selective inhibition, and modulation of Pgp transport are important goals in drug development, but are hindered by a lack of detailed understanding of the drug transport mechanisms (Waghray and Zhang, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citation and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: ATP binding, hydrolysis, and subsequent release of cleaved products fuel large-scale conformational changes in ABC transporters.
source: For Pgp and ABC transporters in general, ATP binding, hydrolysis, and subsequent release of the cleaved products (inorganic phosphate and ADP) fuel large-scale conformational changes that ultimately result in translocation of substrates across the membrane bilayer (Rees et al., 2009; Hofmann et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on ABC transporter mechanisms.

claim: In inward-facing conformations, the nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs) are separated.
source: In inward-facing (IF) conformations, the nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs) are separated, and substrates can access a large binding cavity that is open to the lower membrane leaflet and cytoplasm.
evidence: This describes a structural characteristic of IF conformations based on established knowledge.

claim: In inward-facing conformations, substrates can access a large binding cavity that is open to the lower membrane leaflet and cytoplasm.
source: In inward-facing (IF) conformations, the nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs) are separated, and substrates can access a large binding cavity that is open to the lower membrane leaflet and cytoplasm.
evidence: This describes a structural characteristic of IF conformations based on established knowledge.

claim: ATP-induced dimerization of the NBDs promotes large rearrangements of the transmembrane domains from an IF to an OF conformation.
source: ATP-induced dimerization of the NBDs promotes large rearrangements of the transmembrane domains (TMDs) from an IF to an outward-facing (OF) conformation, from which the substrate is released (Januliene and Moeller, 2020; Verhalen et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research on ABC transporter conformational changes.

claim: Pgp structures with bound substrates and inhibitors in IF conformations have revealed one or more overlapping binding sites.
source: Pgp structures with bound substrates and inhibitors in IF conformations have revealed one or more overlapping binding sites (Aller et al., 2009; Loo and Clarke, 2000; Loo et al., 2009; Alam et al., 2019; Nosol et al., 2020; Szewczyk et al., 2015; Alam et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: Multimodal binding mechanisms for chemically related compounds have been proposed.
source: Multimodal binding mechanisms for chemically related compounds have been proposed (Aller et al., 2009; Chufan et al., 2015), including access of hydrophobic ligands from the lipid-protein interface to the binding sites of Pgp (Nosol et al., 2020; Szewczyk et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research proposing binding mechanisms.

claim: Structural data that elucidate how substrates are shuttled across the lipid bilayer to the extracellular space are unavailable at present.
source: However, structural data that elucidate how substrates are shuttled across the lipid bilayer to the extracellular space are unavailable at present.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field based on the state of prior research.

claim: Only a single OF structure of mammalian Pgp has been described without detectable substrate density.
source: So far, only a single OF structure of mammalian Pgp has been described, but without detectable substrate density (Kim and Chen, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior structural work.

claim: Most insights into the transport pathway arise from molecular dynamics simulations.
source: Most insights into the transport pathway arise from molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, which are also limited by the scarcity of available structural details (Göddeke and Schäfer, 2020; McCormick et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior MD simulation studies.

claim: The authors synthesized a derivative of the QZ-Ala tripeptide substrate by substituting one Ala with Cys disulfide-linked to a 2,4-dinitrophenyl thiolate group (AAC-DNPT).
source: For covalent labeling of Pgp, we synthesized a derivative of the previously published QZ-Ala tripeptide substrate (Szewczyk et al., 2015), by substituting one of the three Ala with Cys that is disulfide-linked to a 2,4-dinitrophenyl thiolate group (designated AAC-DNPT, see Materials and methods, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the synthesis of the compound used in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: QZ-Ala is a strong ATPase stimulator.
source: QZ-Ala is a strong ATPase stimulator and subject to Pgp transport as evidenced by its reduced cytotoxicity in cells overexpressing Pgp (Szewczyk et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research.

claim: QZ-Ala is subject to Pgp transport as evidenced by its reduced cytotoxicity in cells overexpressing Pgp.
source: QZ-Ala is a strong ATPase stimulator and subject to Pgp transport as evidenced by its reduced cytotoxicity in cells overexpressing Pgp (Szewczyk et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research.

claim: The efflux ratio (RE) of QZ-Ala was determined as 2.5.
source: The efflux ratio (RE) of QZ-Ala was determined as 2.5.
evidence: This is experimental data from the MDCK-ABCB1 monolayer permeability assay.

claim: In the presence of the Pgp inhibitor cyclosporin A, the efflux ratio of QZ-Ala was 0.9.
source: In the presence of the Pgp inhibitor cyclosporin A, RE was 0.9, indicating that the Pgp-specific transport of QZ-Ala was inhibited.
evidence: This is experimental data from the MDCK-ABCB1 monolayer permeability assay.

claim: The Pgp-specific transport of QZ-Ala was inhibited by cyclosporin A.
source: In the presence of the Pgp inhibitor cyclosporin A, RE was 0.9, indicating that the Pgp-specific transport of QZ-Ala was inhibited.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data showing reduced efflux ratio.

claim: Four single-Cys mutants of Pgp (Pgp335, Pgp978, Pgp971, and Pgp302) were generated for crosslinking.
source: Four single-Cys mutants of Pgp (Pgp335, Pgp978, Pgp971, and Pgp302) were generated for crosslinking, and mutations were chosen near the two previously reported QZ-Ala binding sites (Szewczyk et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the experimental design and mutant generation.

claim: L335C is located in transmembrane helix 6 (TM6).
source: L335C in transmembrane helix 6 (TM6) and V978C in TM12 are situated at symmetric positions on opposing TMD halves, while L971C is located two helical turns above V978 (Figure 1b).
evidence: This describes the structural location of the mutation with reference to a figure.

claim: V978C is located in TM12.
source: L335C in transmembrane helix 6 (TM6) and V978C in TM12 are situated at symmetric positions on opposing TMD halves, while L971C is located two helical turns above V978 (Figure 1b).
evidence: This describes the structural location of the mutation with reference to a figure.

claim: L335C and V978C are situated at symmetric positions on opposing TMD halves.
source: L335C in transmembrane helix 6 (TM6) and V978C in TM12 are situated at symmetric positions on opposing TMD halves, while L971C is located two helical turns above V978 (Figure 1b).
evidence: This describes the structural relationship between the mutations with reference to a figure.

claim: L971C is located two helical turns above V978.
source: L335C in transmembrane helix 6 (TM6) and V978C in TM12 are situated at symmetric positions on opposing TMD halves, while L971C is located two helical turns above V978 (Figure 1b).
evidence: This describes the structural location of the mutation with reference to a figure.

claim: Pgp335 and Pgp978 reacted with AAC-DNPT within minutes.
source: Based on the appearance of the yellow DNPT byproduct, Pgp335 and Pgp978 reacted with AAC-DNPT within minutes, while Pgp971 and Pgp302 did not.
evidence: This is experimental observation based on the colorimetric assay.

claim: Pgp971 and Pgp302 did not react with AAC-DNPT within minutes.
source: Based on the appearance of the yellow DNPT byproduct, Pgp335 and Pgp978 reacted with AAC-DNPT within minutes, while Pgp971 and Pgp302 did not.
evidence: This is experimental observation based on the colorimetric assay.

claim: After adding Mg2+ ATP, Pgp971 reacted with AAC-DNPT.
source: Only after adding Mg2+ ATP to fuel substrate translocation, Pgp971 reacted with AAC-DNPT, but Pgp302 did not (data not shown).
evidence: This is experimental observation showing ATP-dependent crosslinking.

claim: Pgp302 did not react with AAC-DNPT even after adding Mg2+ ATP.
source: Only after adding Mg2+ ATP to fuel substrate translocation, Pgp971 reacted with AAC-DNPT, but Pgp302 did not (data not shown).
evidence: This is experimental observation.

claim: Covalent attachment of the cyclic peptide AAC was validated by high-resolution mass spectrometry of trypsin-digested peptide fragments.
source: Covalent attachment of the cyclic peptide AAC was further validated by high-resolution mass spectrometry of trypsin-digested peptide fragments (Figure 1—figure supplements 2–4).
evidence: This describes the validation method with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: AAC-DNTP stimulated ATPase activity of CL-Pgp at low concentrations.
source: Similar to QZ-Ala, AAC-DNTP stimulated ATPase activity of CL-Pgp at low concentrations; with half-maximal enhancement of activity (EC50) seen at submicromolar concentrations, suggesting that it also acts as substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays with reference to a figure.

claim: Half-maximal enhancement of ATPase activity (EC50) by AAC-DNTP was seen at submicromolar concentrations.
source: Similar to QZ-Ala, AAC-DNTP stimulated ATPase activity of CL-Pgp at low concentrations; with half-maximal enhancement of activity (EC50) seen at submicromolar concentrations, suggesting that it also acts as substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays with reference to a figure.

claim: AAC-DNTP acts as a substrate for Pgp.
source: Similar to QZ-Ala, AAC-DNTP stimulated ATPase activity of CL-Pgp at low concentrations; with half-maximal enhancement of activity (EC50) seen at submicromolar concentrations, suggesting that it also acts as substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is an inference based on the ATPase stimulation data.

claim: At higher concentrations, the rate of ATP hydrolysis is significantly reduced in the mutants compared to CL-Pgp indicative of crosslinking AAC-DNPT with the single Cys mutants.
source: At higher concentrations, the rate of ATP hydrolysis is significantly reduced in the mutants compared to CL-Pgp indicative of crosslinking AAC-DNPT with the single Cys mutants (Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 5b).
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays with interpretation.

claim: Pgp335 and Pgp978 retain notably higher ATPase activity after crosslinking than the respective apo-Pgp mutants in the absence of substrate.
source: Importantly, Pgp335 and Pgp978 retain notably higher ATPase activity after crosslinking than the respective apo-Pgp mutants in the absence of substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b and Figure 1d), suggesting that tethered AAC still acts as a substrate and that Pgp335 and Pgp978 cycle between IF and OF conformations.
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays with reference to figures.

claim: Tethered AAC still acts as a substrate in Pgp335 and Pgp978.
source: Importantly, Pgp335 and Pgp978 retain notably higher ATPase activity after crosslinking than the respective apo-Pgp mutants in the absence of substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b and Figure 1d), suggesting that tethered AAC still acts as a substrate and that Pgp335 and Pgp978 cycle between IF and OF conformations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ATPase activity data.

claim: Pgp335 and Pgp978 cycle between IF and OF conformations.
source: Importantly, Pgp335 and Pgp978 retain notably higher ATPase activity after crosslinking than the respective apo-Pgp mutants in the absence of substrate (Figure 1—figure supplement 5b and Figure 1d), suggesting that tethered AAC still acts as a substrate and that Pgp335 and Pgp978 cycle between IF and OF conformations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the ATPase activity data.

claim: The IF structure of Pgp335 was solved at 3.8 Å resolution.
source: The IF structure of Pgp335, solved at 3.8 Å resolution, shows clear densities for two substrate molecules: one crosslinked and one not (IF335-2lig, Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis.

claim: The IF structure of Pgp335 shows clear densities for two substrate molecules: one crosslinked and one not.
source: The IF structure of Pgp335, solved at 3.8 Å resolution, shows clear densities for two substrate molecules: one crosslinked and one not (IF335-2lig, Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The non-crosslinked molecule in IF335-2lig is bound in a position that resembles the one previously reported in a crystal structure.
source: The non-crosslinked molecule is bound in a position that resembles the one previously reported in a crystal structure (Szewczyk et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current structure with prior structural data.

claim: The non-crosslinked substrate interacts closely with the covalently linked substrate in IF335-2lig.
source: It interacts closely with the covalently linked substrate, which is situated further up the membrane.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: Both ligand molecules in IF335-2lig are oriented along the vertical axis of the protein and positioned side-by-side through hydrophobic interactions.
source: Both ligand molecules are oriented along the vertical axis of the protein and positioned side-by-side through hydrophobic interactions.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: Two substrate molecules are bound in the IF structure of Pgp978 (IF978-2lig).
source: Two substrate molecules are also bound in the IF structure of Pgp978 (IF978-2lig); the non-covalently bound molecule is clearly visible at a similar position as in IF335-2lig, while the crosslinked substrate is located on the opposite side of the binding cavity near TM12 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: In IF978-2lig, the non-covalently bound molecule is at a similar position as in IF335-2lig.
source: Two substrate molecules are also bound in the IF structure of Pgp978 (IF978-2lig); the non-covalently bound molecule is clearly visible at a similar position as in IF335-2lig, while the crosslinked substrate is located on the opposite side of the binding cavity near TM12 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a comparison of structural data between two structures.

claim: In IF978-2lig, the crosslinked substrate is located on the opposite side of the binding cavity near TM12.
source: Two substrate molecules are also bound in the IF structure of Pgp978 (IF978-2lig); the non-covalently bound molecule is clearly visible at a similar position as in IF335-2lig, while the crosslinked substrate is located on the opposite side of the binding cavity near TM12 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: The IF structure of Pgp971 (IF971-1lig) was solved at 4.3 Å resolution.
source: Corroborating our labeling data (Figure 1c), in the IF structure of Pgp971 (IF971-1lig) at 4.3 Å resolution, only the non-crosslinked substrate is bound at the approximate location seen for non-crosslinked substrate in IF335-2lig and IF978-2lig (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 4e).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis.

claim: In IF971-1lig, only the non-crosslinked substrate is bound.
source: Corroborating our labeling data (Figure 1c), in the IF structure of Pgp971 (IF971-1lig) at 4.3 Å resolution, only the non-crosslinked substrate is bound at the approximate location seen for non-crosslinked substrate in IF335-2lig and IF978-2lig (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 4e).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Multi-model cryoEM analyses of ATP-bound Pgp335 revealed three different OF conformations within a single dataset.
source: Multi-model cryoEM analyses of ATP-bound Pgp335 revealed three different OF conformations within a single dataset: ligand-free (40.4%), single-ligand-bound (33.3%), and double-ligand-bound (26.4%) (OF335-nolig, OF335-1lig, and OF335-2lig), at 2.6 Å, 2.6 Å, and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 2).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to figures.

claim: OF335-nolig represents 40.4% of the particles in the Pgp335 dataset.
source: Multi-model cryoEM analyses of ATP-bound Pgp335 revealed three different OF conformations within a single dataset: ligand-free (40.4%), single-ligand-bound (33.3%), and double-ligand-bound (26.4%) (OF335-nolig, OF335-1lig, and OF335-2lig), at 2.6 Å, 2.6 Å, and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 2).
evidence: This is data from cryoEM particle classification.

source: Multi-model cryoEM analyses of ATP-bound Pgp335 revealed three different OF conformations within a single dataset: ligand-free (40.4%), single-ligand-bound (33.3%), and double-ligand-bound (26.4%) (OF335-nolig, OF335-1lig, and OF335-2lig), at 2.6 Å, 2.6 Å, and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 2).

source: Multi-model cryoEM analyses of ATP-bound Pgp335 revealed three different OF conformations within a single dataset: ligand-free (40.4%), single-ligand-bound (33.3%), and double-ligand-bound (26.4%) (OF335-nolig, OF335-1lig, and OF335-2lig), at 2.6 Å, 2.6 Å, and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 2).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis.

source: Multi-model cryoEM analyses of ATP-bound Pgp335 revealed three different OF conformations within a single dataset: ligand-free (40.4%), single-ligand-bound (33.3%), and double-ligand-bound (26.4%) (OF335-nolig, OF335-1lig, and OF335-2lig), at 2.6 Å, 2.6 Å, and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 2).

source: Multi-model cryoEM analyses of ATP-bound Pgp335 revealed three different OF conformations within a single dataset: ligand-free (40.4%), single-ligand-bound (33.3%), and double-ligand-bound (26.4%) (OF335-nolig, OF335-1lig, and OF335-2lig), at 2.6 Å, 2.6 Å, and 3.1 Å resolution, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Figure 2).

claim: For Pgp978, only OF conformations with a single bound ligand (OF978-1lig) were captured at 2.9 Å resolution.
source: For Pgp978 and Pgp971, only OF conformations with a single bound ligand (OF978-1lig and OF971-1lig, Figure 2) were captured at 2.9 Å and 3 Å resolution, respectively.
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: For Pgp971, only OF conformations with a single bound ligand (OF971-1lig) were captured at 3 Å resolution.
source: For Pgp978 and Pgp971, only OF conformations with a single bound ligand (OF978-1lig and OF971-1lig, Figure 2) were captured at 2.9 Å and 3 Å resolution, respectively.
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: In the OF structures with a single bound substrate, the central transmembrane helices TM1, TM6, TM7, and TM12 bulge outward to accommodate the substrate in a small tunnel.
source: In the OF structures with a single bound substrate, the central transmembrane helices TM1, TM6, TM7, and TM12 bulge outward to accommodate the substrate in a small tunnel (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data with reference to a figure.

claim: Comparing IF335-2lig to OF335-1lig, the covalently attached ligand pivots around the Cys residue by almost 180°.
source: Comparing the ligand positions between the IF and OF structures, in IF335-2lig to OF335-1lig, and IF978-2lig to OF978-1lig, the covalently attached ligand pivots around the respective Cys residue by almost 180°, moving it further up the translocation tunnel (Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 4a, b, and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a structural comparison between IF and OF conformations with reference to figures and videos.

claim: Comparing IF978-2lig to OF978-1lig, the covalently attached ligand pivots around the Cys residue by almost 180°.
source: Comparing the ligand positions between the IF and OF structures, in IF335-2lig to OF335-1lig, and IF978-2lig to OF978-1lig, the covalently attached ligand pivots around the respective Cys residue by almost 180°, moving it further up the translocation tunnel (Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 4a, b, and Videos 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a structural comparison between IF and OF conformations with reference to figures and videos.

claim: The ligand position and orientation in OF335-1lig and OF978-1lig overall coincide well.
source: The ligand position and orientation in OF335-1lig and OF978-1lig overall coincide well, with the latter shifting up slightly (Figure 2—figure supplement 4d).
evidence: This is a structural comparison between two OF conformations with reference to a figure.

claim: The export tunnel is inherent to substrate translocation regardless of the initial binding position in the IF conformation.
source: This finding indicates that the export tunnel is inherent to substrate translocation regardless of the initial binding position in the IF conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural comparison of ligand positions.

claim: The data suggest a single common pathway for substrate export in Pgp.
source: As such, our data suggest a single common pathway for substrate export in Pgp, contrary to the dual pseudosymmetric pathways suggested earlier (McCormick et al., 2015; Parveen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data, contrasted with prior models.

claim: OF971-1lig captures a later-stage transport intermediate.
source: OF971-1lig captures a later-stage transport intermediate, in which the compound resides approximately 7 Å further up the translocation tunnel and is coordinated by highly conserved residues, including M74 and F78 (Figures 2 and 3b, Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 7).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data with reference to figures.

claim: In OF971-1lig, the compound resides approximately 7 Å further up the translocation tunnel compared to earlier intermediates.
source: OF971-1lig captures a later-stage transport intermediate, in which the compound resides approximately 7 Å further up the translocation tunnel and is coordinated by highly conserved residues, including M74 and F78 (Figures 2 and 3b, Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 7).
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the cryoEM data with reference to figures.

claim: In OF971-1lig, the substrate is coordinated by highly conserved residues, including M74 and F78.
source: OF971-1lig captures a later-stage transport intermediate, in which the compound resides approximately 7 Å further up the translocation tunnel and is coordinated by highly conserved residues, including M74 and F78 (Figures 2 and 3b, Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 7).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data with reference to figures.

claim: The substrate was likely transported to residue L971C before the crosslinking reaction could take place in OF971-1lig.
source: As no crosslinked substrate was detected in the corresponding IF structure, the substrate was likely transported to residue L971C before the crosslinking reaction could take place.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of crosslinked substrate in the IF structure.

claim: Substrate entry from the extracellular side is less likely given the small opening of the substrate translocation pathway in all OF Pgp structures.
source: Substrate entry from the extracellular side is less likely given the small opening of the substrate translocation pathway in all OF Pgp structures with or without bound substrate obtained here and previously (Kim and Chen, 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations from current and prior studies.

claim: In all substrate-bound OF conformations, methionines and phenylalanines at different positions are important for ligand coordination.
source: In all substrate-bound OF conformations, methionines and phenylalanines at different positions seem to be important for ligand coordination in all of the Pgp structures (Figure 2—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data with reference to a figure.

claim: The substrate is held in the binding pocket mainly by hydrophobic interactions throughout the different conformations.
source: As expected, the substrate is held in the binding pocket mainly by the hydrophobic interactions throughout the different conformations (Figure 2—figure supplements 3 and 7).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data with reference to figures.

claim: In the OF335-nolig structure, the translocation tunnel is collapsed.
source: In the OF335-nolig structure, as well as in the virtually indistinguishable control, the translocation tunnel is collapsed, which shields the substrate binding pocket from the extracellular milieu and prevents re-entry from this side (Kim and Chen, 2018).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data with citation to prior work.

claim: The collapsed translocation tunnel in OF335-nolig shields the substrate binding pocket from the extracellular milieu and prevents re-entry from this side.
source: In the OF335-nolig structure, as well as in the virtually indistinguishable control, the translocation tunnel is collapsed, which shields the substrate binding pocket from the extracellular milieu and prevents re-entry from this side (Kim and Chen, 2018).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural observation with citation to prior work.

claim: In IF conformations, TM1 is a long, straight helix.
source: In IF conformations, TM1 is a long, straight helix (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data with reference to figures.

claim: In OF335-1lig, OF978-1lig, and OF971-1lig, TM1 swings out at A63, dilating the transmembrane passage.
source: However, in OF335-1lig, OF978-1lig, and OF971-1lig, TM1 swings out at A63, dilating the transmembrane passage and providing sufficient space for accommodating the bound ligand.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: In OF335-1lig, OF978-1lig, and OF971-1lig, a pronounced kink at G72 on TM1 destabilizes the helix.
source: At the same time, a pronounced kink at G72 on TM1 destabilizes the helix and the extracellular loop of Pgp between TM1 and TM2 and leads to a partial unwinding.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The kink at G72 leads to partial unwinding of TM1 and the extracellular loop between TM1 and TM2.
source: At the same time, a pronounced kink at G72 on TM1 destabilizes the helix and the extracellular loop of Pgp between TM1 and TM2 and leads to a partial unwinding.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data.

claim: The conformational deformation of TM1 shields the intramembranous tunnel from the extracellular environment, with TM1 acting as a lid.
source: This conformational deformation shields the intramembranous tunnel from the extracellular environment, with TM1 acting as a lid, almost parallel to the membrane (Figures 2 and 4a, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural observation with reference to figures.

claim: Along with the upward movement of the ligand, the TM1 loop is progressively lifted and restabilized.
source: Strikingly, along with the upward movement of the ligand (from L335C to V978C to L971C), the TM1 loop is progressively lifted and restabilized.
evidence: This is a structural observation comparing multiple structures.

claim: The helix is straightened upon the release of the ligand in OF335-nolig.
source: Ultimately, as shown previously (Kim and Chen, 2018) and by our OF335-nolig structure, the helix is straightened upon the release of the ligand (Figure 4a, Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the current data and prior work with reference to figures.

claim: The extracellular gate is sealed in all OF structures.
source: Interestingly, the extracellular gate is sealed in all OF structures, which is especially surprising for OF971-1lig where the ligand is near the tunnel exit (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the cryoEM data with reference to figures.

claim: In MD simulations starting from OF978-1lig at T=400 K, movement and release of the non-covalently bound substrate to the extracellular side was observed.
source: In simulations starting from OF978-1lig at T=400 K, we observed movement and release of the non-covalently bound substrate to the extracellular side moderated by interactions between the ligand and hydrophobic residues in the upper part of TM1 (Video 3).
evidence: This is data from MD simulations with reference to a video.

claim: The substrate release in MD simulations was moderated by interactions between the ligand and hydrophobic residues in the upper part of TM1.
source: In simulations starting from OF978-1lig at T=400 K, we observed movement and release of the non-covalently bound substrate to the extracellular side moderated by interactions between the ligand and hydrophobic residues in the upper part of TM1 (Video 3).
evidence: This is data from MD simulations with reference to a video.

claim: The intermediate steps in MD simulations coincided well with the conformations observed in cryoEM.
source: The intermediate steps coincided well with the conformations observed in cryoEM (Figure 4, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a comparison between MD simulation results and cryoEM structures with reference to figures.

claim: Without any bias imposed, the substrate in MD simulations progressed to a position closely matching OF971-1lig.
source: Without any bias imposed, the substrate progressed to a position closely matching OF971-1lig (Figures 2 and 4b).
evidence: This is data from MD simulations compared to cryoEM structure with reference to figures.

claim: While TM1 gradually refolded from the intracellular side, the substrate wiggled out to form transient interactions with the still unstructured extracellular part of TM1.
source: Then, while TM1 gradually refolded from the intracellular side, the substrate wiggled out to form transient interactions with the still unstructured extracellular part of TM1 (Figure 4).
evidence: This is data from MD simulations with reference to a figure.

claim: The substrate escaped without Pgp experiencing a wide opening of the extracellular region in MD simulations.
source: Importantly, the substrate escaped without Pgp experiencing a wide opening of the extracellular region.
evidence: This is a key observation from MD simulations.

claim: After the substrate left the exit tunnel, TM1 continued to refold to attain a straight helix configuration like OF335-nolig at the end of the simulation.
source: After the substrate left the exit tunnel, TM1 continued to refold to attain a straight helix configuration like OF335-nolig at the end of the simulation (Figure 4).
evidence: This is data from MD simulations with reference to a figure.

claim: In a simulation starting from OF335-1lig performed at T=330 K, a similar release pathway was observed.
source: In a simulation starting from OF335-1lig performed at T=330 K, a similar release pathway was observed (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is data from MD simulations with reference to a figure.

claim: With exception of TM1, motions in Pgp to accommodate the moving substrate were mostly limited to small dilations of the transmembrane helices.
source: Overall, with exception of TM1, motions in Pgp to accommodate the moving substrate were mostly limited to small dilations of the transmembrane helices, supporting our observations from cryoEM.
evidence: This is a summary observation from MD simulations compared to cryoEM data.

claim: Glycine 72 is highly conserved in mammalian Pgp.
source: Our cryoEM structures and MD simulations revealed an important regulatory role of TM1 during substrate transport, emphasizing the helix-breaking G72. Therefore, we mutated this residue, which is highly conserved in mammalian Pgp (Figure 3), to a helix-stabilizing alanine (López-Llano et al., 2006) and tested the mutant's ability to export structurally diverse fungicides and to convey drug resistance in vivo.
evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment data shown in a figure.

claim: The G72A mutant expressed normally in S. cerevisiae.
source: Compared to the wild-type and CL-Pgp, the G72A mutant expressed normally in S. cerevisiae (Figure 3c), but showed significantly reduced growth resistance to the test drugs including doxorubicin, FK506, and valinomycin (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is experimental data from expression analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: The G72A mutant showed significantly reduced growth resistance to doxorubicin, FK506, and valinomycin.
source: Compared to the wild-type and CL-Pgp, the G72A mutant expressed normally in S. cerevisiae (Figure 3c), but showed significantly reduced growth resistance to the test drugs including doxorubicin, FK506, and valinomycin (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is experimental data from drug resistance assays with reference to a figure.

claim: The G72A mutant displayed only low levels of basal ATPase activity.
source: In presence of transport substrates such as FK506, valinomycin, or verapamil, the ATPase activity of WT Pgp was significantly stimulated; however, the G72A mutant displayed only low levels of basal ATPase activity (in the absence of drug) and the response to drug stimulation was greatly diminished over a range of concentrations tested (Figure 3e–g).
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays with reference to figures.

claim: The response to drug stimulation was greatly diminished in the G72A mutant over a range of concentrations tested.
source: In presence of transport substrates such as FK506, valinomycin, or verapamil, the ATPase activity of WT Pgp was significantly stimulated; however, the G72A mutant displayed only low levels of basal ATPase activity (in the absence of drug) and the response to drug stimulation was greatly diminished over a range of concentrations tested (Figure 3e–g).
evidence: This is experimental data from ATPase assays with reference to figures.

claim: CryoEM on the Pgp335 G72A mutant revealed two conformations after multi-model classification.
source: To reveal potential structural consequences responsible for the loss of function, we performed cryoEM on the Pgp335 G72A mutant after crosslinking the single cysteine L335C with AAC-DNTP and stabilizing the OF complex with Mg2+ ATP and vanadate in a post-hydrolysis intermediate state. After multi-model classification, two conformations emerged.
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis.

claim: The first conformation of the G72A mutant was resolved at 3.0 Å and shows no substrate bound.
source: The first conformation, resolved at 3.0 Å, shows no substrate bound in analogy to OF335-nolig.
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis.

claim: The second dominant conformation of the G72A mutant is much more heterogenous, resulting in a reduced and anisotropic resolution of approximately 4.6 Å.
source: The second dominant conformation is, however, much more heterogenous, resulting in a reduced and anisotropic resolution of approximately 4.6 Å (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: In the second conformation of the G72A mutant, the NBDs are well resolved but several transmembrane helices are missing, including TM1.
source: Here, the NBDs are well resolved but several transmembrane helices are missing, including TM1 in which residue G72A is located.
evidence: This is structural data from cryoEM analysis.

claim: The structural disorder observed in the transmembrane region of the G72A mutant is likely a result of the tethered ligand causing local distortion.
source: The structural disorder, observed in the transmembrane region, is likely a result of the tethered ligand, causing local distortion of the surrounding α-helices as TM1 may not be able to kink at G72 in the mutant, which could explain its impaired transport function.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: TM1 may not be able to kink at G72 in the G72A mutant, which could explain its impaired transport function.
source: The structural disorder, observed in the transmembrane region, is likely a result of the tethered ligand, causing local distortion of the surrounding α-helices as TM1 may not be able to kink at G72 in the mutant, which could explain its impaired transport function.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural and functional data.

claim: Transport commences in the IF conformation with binding of the substrate.
source: Our data suggest a mechanism for how Pgp mediates substrate transport. Transport commences in the IF conformation with binding of the substrate.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the structural data.

claim: Upon ATP-induced NBD dimerization, the transporter converges into an OF conformation in which the intracellular gate is closed.
source: Upon ATP-induced NBD dimerization, the transporter converges into an OF conformation in which the intracellular gate is closed.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the structural data.

claim: The presence of the substrate in the OF conformation dislocates TM1 at A63 and introduces a sharp kink at G72.
source: The presence of the substrate in the OF conformation of Pgp dislocates TM1 at A63 and introduces a sharp kink at G72, forcing the helix to unwind partially between TM1 and TM2 (Figure 4 and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the structural data with reference to figures.

claim: The kink at G72 enlarges the extracellular loop which shields the transmembrane tunnel from the extracellular environment.
source: This enlarges the extracellular loop which shields the transmembrane tunnel from the extracellular environment and guides the substrate to move up the translocation tunnel, allowing TM1 to gradually restabilize.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the structural data.

claim: During the last stages of transport, the TM1-TM2 regulatory loop straightens.
source: During the last stages of transport (OF971-1lig to OF335-nolig), the TM1-TM2 regulatory loop straightens, and the substrate-interacting hydrophobic residues (M74 and F78) rotate and pivot away from the tunnel, which facilitates the escape of the substrate from the transporter.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the structural data.

claim: The substrate-interacting hydrophobic residues M74 and F78 rotate and pivot away from the tunnel during the last stages of transport.
source: During the last stages of transport (OF971-1lig to OF335-nolig), the TM1-TM2 regulatory loop straightens, and the substrate-interacting hydrophobic residues (M74 and F78) rotate and pivot away from the tunnel, which facilitates the escape of the substrate from the transporter.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the structural data.

claim: The proposed TM1 kinking and straightening mechanism would obviate the requirement for the Y-shaped, wide-open OF conformation reported for multiple bacterial ABC transporters.
source: Notwithstanding, the proposed TM1 kinking and straightening mechanism of substrate expulsion would obviate the requirement for the Y-shaped, wide-open OF conformation reported for multiple bacterial ABC transporters (Ward et al., 2007; Dawson and Locher, 2006), suggesting a substrate-dependent transport mechanism in Pgp, or else a divergence of mechanisms among ABC transporters.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mechanism in the context of prior models with citations.

claim: The data suggest a substrate-dependent transport mechanism in Pgp, or else a divergence of mechanisms among ABC transporters.
source: Notwithstanding, the proposed TM1 kinking and straightening mechanism of substrate expulsion would obviate the requirement for the Y-shaped, wide-open OF conformation reported for multiple bacterial ABC transporters (Ward et al., 2007; Dawson and Locher, 2006), suggesting a substrate-dependent transport mechanism in Pgp, or else a divergence of mechanisms among ABC transporters.
evidence: This is speculation based on the proposed mechanism and comparison with other transporters.

claim: The hydrophobic nature of the substrate promotes the binding of two substrate molecules to each other in OF335-2lig.
source: For the OF335-2lig structure, observed in the same dataset as OF335-1lig and OF335-nolig, we hypothesize that the hydrophobic nature of the substrate promotes the binding of two substrate molecules to each other.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural observation.

claim: MD simulations with OF335-2lig as a starting conformation reveal no separation of the two molecules.
source: MD simulations with this structure as a starting conformation reveal no separation of the two molecules, suggesting that they might be treated as one bigger substrate in the transport event.
evidence: This is data from MD simulations.

claim: The two substrate molecules in OF335-2lig might be treated as one bigger substrate in the transport event.
source: MD simulations with this structure as a starting conformation reveal no separation of the two molecules, suggesting that they might be treated as one bigger substrate in the transport event.
evidence: This is speculation based on MD simulation results.

claim: The scarcity of high-resolution structures of substrate-bound OF conformations has severely limited understanding of substrate translocation in ABC transporters.
source: How ABC transporters move substrates through the lipid bilayer has been a long-standing question (Fan et al., 2020). The scarcity of high-resolution structures of substrate-bound OF conformations (Chaptal et al., 2022), especially in the highly transient intermediate states, has severely limited our understanding of this vital process.
evidence: This identifies a knowledge gap in the field with citations.

claim: The authors determined eight high-resolution structures of Pgp revealing the molecular mechanics of substrate translocation.
source: Here, we were able to determine eight high-resolution structures of the archetypical ABC transporter Pgp, revealing the underlying molecular mechanics of substrate translocation.
evidence: This summarizes the primary achievement of the study.

claim: The large number and diversity of ABC transporters make it unlikely that a universal substrate translocation mechanism will emerge.
source: In general, the large number and diversity of ABC transporters, and the even wider variety of their substrates, make it unlikely that a universal substrate translocation mechanism will emerge.
evidence: This is speculation based on knowledge of ABC transporter diversity.

claim: The strategy of stalling transient intermediates through crosslinking and cryoEM analysis could serve as a blueprint to understand transport mechanisms of other ABC transporters.
source: Our strategy of stalling the otherwise highly transient intermediates in this process through crosslinking and subsequent high-resolution cryoEM analysis could serve as a blueprint to understand the transport mechanisms of lipid transporters as well as other members of the transporter family.
evidence: This is a proposal for future applications of the methodology.
